name: Nova
role: Our ticket-to-PR agent: plans, builds and opens a PR.
plain: Nova is a program that runs Claude with tools on a fresh machine and turns one Jira ticket into one pull request. A person assigns the ticket to Nova, approves its plan, and a different person approves its PR.

name: Byte
role: Our PR review agent; also reviews Nova's draft PRs.
plain: Byte already reviews pull requests in the product repo and leaves comments on bugs it finds. It reviews Nova's drafts too, and it stays independent of Nova's own self-review.

name: Routine
role: Nova with a different trigger and a written charter.
plain: A routine is the same agent as Nova, started by an event such as a red build or a bug ticket instead of an assignment. A short YAML file, its charter, says what it may touch and who owns it.

name: CI fixer (cifix)
role: Routine that makes one fix when CI goes red on main.
plain: When a CI workflow fails on main, one CI fixer run per root cause reproduces the failure on a fresh machine and makes the smallest fix. If the failure is not in the code, it hands the problem to a person.

name: Upgrade fixer
role: Routine that repairs a failed Renovate dependency PR.
plain: When a dependency update opened by Renovate fails CI, an upgrade fixer tries to repair that one PR. There is one for frontend npm packages, one for Python packages and one for infrastructure.

name: Flaky-test fixer
role: Routine that fixes the cause of a flaky backend test.
plain: A flaky test passes sometimes and fails sometimes. This routine looks for the real cause, fixes it, and proves the test then passes about 50 times in a row.

name: Bug fixer
role: Routine that fixes a triaged Bug ticket, reproducing it first.
plain: A bug fixer picks up a Bug ticket that a team has triaged, reproduces the bug first, and fixes it with a test that proves it. There is one for the frontend and one for the backend.

name: Code-health routines
role: Weekly routines: dead code, test gaps, duplicates, brain ingest.
plain: These routines run on a schedule instead of on an event. They remove dead code, add missing tests, propose merging duplicates, and update brain pages from merged work.

name: Security fixer
role: Routine that bumps a package to its fixed release.
plain: When a security finding has a fixed release of the affected package, this routine opens the version bump. Findings without a fixed release stay with people.

name: QA agent
role: Co-signs the QA plan, then tests the app in a browser.
plain: Before code, the QA agent reads only the ticket and the planned checks and asks for anything missing. After the build, it uses the running app in a browser like a tester and records a short video per check.

name: Self-reviewer
role: Fresh-context reviewer that reads Nova's diff and writes a receipt.
plain: A second model session that never saw Nova's reasoning reads the change and lists important problems. What it found and what Nova fixed go into the PR as a receipt.

name: Scope judge
role: Judge that vetoes changes the ticket did not ask for.
plain: The scope judge sees only the ticket text and the final diff. It can veto unrelated refactors and weakened tests before the PR leaves draft.

name: PR judge
role: Judge that checks every claim in the PR description.
plain: The PR judge reads the PR description the way a reviewer from another team would. It flags any claim that the diff or the proof does not support.

name: Vanil
role: Nave's compliance agent on n8n; tracks security policy work.
plain: Vanil is an older agent built in n8n that files security and compliance findings in Jira. The new platform does not replace it; the brain points to it instead of copying its data.

name: Rhino Brain bot
role: Slack bot that answers questions from brain pages, with citations.
plain: People mention the bot in a public Slack channel and it answers from the brain pages, citing where each fact comes from. It is read-only and says when it does not know.

name: rhino-ai-agents[bot]
role: The GitHub App every agent pushes and opens PRs with.
plain: All agent branches and PRs on GitHub come from this one identity, so rules can treat agent work differently. It cannot merge, has no bypass, and has no permission to change CI workflow files.

name: Nova (Jira user)
role: Jira service account; assigning a ticket to it hands work over.
plain: Nova has its own user in Jira so people can assign tickets to it like to a teammate. Its token stays with the services outside the machine; the machine never sees it.

name: Slack app
role: Our Slack app: /nova commands, plan buttons, one thread per ticket.
plain: The Slack app gives people commands like /nova RH-1234 and the Approve, Change and Stop buttons. It keeps one thread per ticket with a status message that is edited in place.

name: Renovate
role: Bot that opens grouped dependency-update PRs every month.
plain: Renovate reads the package files and opens PRs that bump dependency versions. When one of its PRs fails CI, an upgrade fixer tries to repair it.

name: Orchestrator
role: Temporal worker that runs every agent workflow and starts every run.
plain: The orchestrator is our service on the internal cluster that runs the workflows: it claims machines, waits for people and releases machines. Only the orchestrator may start an agent run.

name: Temporal
role: Workflow engine: saves each step so runs survive restarts and waits.
plain: Temporal runs functions called workflows and saves their progress after every step. A run can wait days for a person, survive a deploy, and carry on where it stopped.

name: ticketToPr
role: The Temporal workflow for one Nova ticket, from plan to PR.
plain: ticketToPr is the function that drives one Nova run: plan on a small machine, wait for approval, build on a bigger one, open the PR. It always gives its machines back at the end.

name: routineRun
role: The Temporal workflow every routine runs.
plain: routineRun is the routines' version of ticketToPr: it loads the charter, gathers triggers, checks the gates, works on a fresh machine and ships the PR the same way Nova does.

name: Harness (nova-worker)
role: Our program inside the VM that runs the Claude session.
plain: The harness is the code around the model: it reads the task, starts a Claude Agent SDK session and adds our tools and hooks. It runs inside the sandbox VM and talks only to the gateway and the broker.

name: Claude Code / Agent SDK
role: Anthropic's agent program and library that the harness runs.
plain: Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent, and the Agent SDK lets our code run it as a library with our own tools and hooks. A pinned copy is baked into the machine image.

name: Broker
role: Holds GitHub, Jira and Slack credentials; makes those calls for runs.
plain: The machine never holds a key. When the agent wants to push, comment or post, it asks the broker, which checks that the run is allowed to do it and then makes the call itself.

name: LLM gateway
role: Adds the Anthropic key to each model call and counts the cost.
plain: Every model call from the machine goes to the gateway with a short-lived run token instead of a key. The gateway swaps in the real key, streams the answer back and records the spend per run and ticket.

name: Egress proxy (Squid)
role: The only way out to the internet, through a short allow-list.
plain: Egress means traffic leaving the network. The sandbox machines can reach the internet only through this proxy, which allows a short list of sites, so injected instructions have nowhere to send our code.

name: PrivateLink path
role: Private network path from the VMs to broker, gateway and collector.
plain: PrivateLink is an AWS feature that connects two private networks without the internet. The sandbox machines use it to reach only three services: the broker, the gateway and the telemetry collector.

name: Vault
role: Secret store; keys go from it to services, never to VMs.
plain: Vault is where our keys and tokens live, such as the GitHub App key and the Jira token. A sync tool called External Secrets copies them into the services that need them.

name: Jira poll
role: Asks Jira every minute for tickets assigned to Nova.
plain: Instead of Jira calling us, a scheduled job asks Jira every minute which tickets are assigned to Nova. For each one it starts a run, or joins the one already open.

name: Trigger service
role: Turns a red CI run into one routine run per root cause.
plain: A small Action in the product repo tells this internal service when CI fails. The service re-reads the failure and starts one routine run per root cause, or adds the event to the open one.

name: Slots (the VM line)
role: Fixed number of VMs each agent may run at once.
plain: Each agent may run only a few machines at the same time, for example three for Nova. Extra work waits in line until a run gives a slot back.

name: Kill switch
role: Stops one agent's runs and new starts at once.
plain: The kill switch is a flag per agent that every run reads before each step. Turning it on ends that agent's runs cleanly, refuses new ones and makes its model tokens useless.

name: Sandbox VM
role: The fresh machine one run works on; destroyed after the run.
plain: Each run gets its own new virtual machine (VM) in a separate AWS account, built from one prepared image. It holds no keys and is never reused.

name: Warm pool
role: Stopped, ready VMs waiting so a run gets one in a minute.
plain: A warm pool keeps a few prepared machines switched off but ready. A run takes one and has it running in about a minute instead of building one from scratch.

name: Sweeper
role: Job every 15 minutes that destroys leftover VMs and disks.
plain: If a run crashes or the orchestrator is down, a machine could be left running. The sweeper finds such machines by their tags and destroys them.

name: Progress watcher
role: Spots loops in a run and answers with a ladder of nudges.
plain: The watcher reads every tool call and checks whether the run makes real progress. When it sees a loop it steps in one rung at a time, from a nudge up to a question to a person.

name: Cost backstop
role: Far-away cost line where a run pauses between turns and asks.
plain: A normal ticket never reaches it. If a run spends far more than usual, it pauses between turns and asks a person whether to continue; at first it only logs.

name: FCP Lab
role: The full product stack on one machine, with fake seed data.
plain: FCP Lab runs the whole product on one machine so changes can be tested for real. It is baked into the sandbox image and runs with fake data only.

name: Telemetry collector
role: Receives traces and metrics and strips content before storing.
plain: The collector takes in OpenTelemetry signals from laptops and agent machines. It removes prompt text and personal details, then stores metrics and events.

name: VictoriaMetrics / VictoriaLogs
role: Where metrics and logs are stored for dashboards and alerts.
plain: VictoriaMetrics stores numbers over time and VictoriaLogs stores log lines. Dashboards and alert rules read from them.

name: Grafana
role: Dashboards: operations, spend, evals and delivery.
plain: Grafana draws charts from the stored metrics. We build dashboards for running agents, spend, eval scores and delivery speed.

name: Nightly metrics job
role: Nightly job that turns PRs, tickets and CI runs into team metrics.
plain: Every night it reads pull requests, Jira tickets and CI runs, and writes team-level delivery numbers. It never reports on single people.

name: Independent-approval check
role: Required check: someone other than the requester must approve.
plain: GitHub cannot know who asked for an agent's PR, because the agent is the author. This check reads the Requested-by line and fails if the only approval comes from that person.

name: Locked checks
role: Stops agents changing the tests and CI they are judged by.
plain: Agents may add tests but may not edit CI workflows, lint settings or the tests approved in their plan. A hook refuses the edit in the machine and a required check fails the PR if one slips through.

name: fcp main ruleset
role: GitHub rules on main: one approval, required checks, no bypass for agents.
plain: A ruleset is GitHub's set of rules for a branch. On the product repo's main branch it asks for exactly one approval and green required checks, and only a small break-glass team can bypass it.

name: n8n
role: Older workflow tool where Vanil and business flows run.
plain: n8n is a visual automation tool running on the internal cluster. It keeps running business workflows; agent work moves to the new platform.

name: Nexus
role: Internal package mirror; the one site the proxy allows by default.
plain: Nexus mirrors npm and Python packages inside our network. It is the only site on the egress proxy's starting allow-list.

name: Harbor
role: Python tool that runs benchmark tasks against an agent.
plain: Harbor runs a set of benchmark tasks through an agent and scores the results. Our ticket benchmark uses it with a small adapter for Nova.

name: kb search tool
role: Command and agent tool that searches brain pages and cites them.
plain: The kb tool searches the brain pages and returns answers with the page they came from. People use it as a command; Nova uses it as its kb_search tool.

name: Jev (TypeSafe)
role: Outside model Byte uses for its cheap first-pass sniff.
plain: TypeSafe is an outside company and Jev is its model. Byte uses it for a quick first look before the full review.

name: inf-rhinohealth (inf)
role: Our Kubernetes cluster for internal tools, where the services run.
plain: inf is a group of machines that runs containers for internal tools. The orchestrator, broker, gateway, Slack app and Temporal all run there, outside the sandbox VMs.

name: ai-agents AWS account
role: Separate AWS account where the sandbox VMs live.
plain: All agent machines run in their own AWS account, apart from the product. Its network has no route out except through the egress proxy.

name: fcp repo
role: The product monorepo; agents work here, the platform does not live here.
plain: fcp holds the product: the Django backend, the on-prem client, the Python SDK and the frontend. Nova's and the routines' PRs land here.

name: ai-agents repo
role: The platform's TypeScript repo: gateway, broker, orchestrator, harness.
plain: One repo with one npm workspace per service, plus a small Python corner for evals. Every platform ticket's code lands here.

name: infrastructure repo
role: OpenTofu and Terragrunt code for our cloud and internal services.
plain: This repo builds the cloud: accounts, networks, machine images and the deployments on the internal cluster. Only DevOps approves its PRs and only people apply it.

name: gitops repo
role: Argo CD apps and Helm charts for the product clusters only.
plain: gitops deploys the product, not the agent platform. Agents never sync it; people do.

name: claude-plugins repo
role: Private plugin marketplace with our skills and hooks.
plain: It holds plugins such as rhino-core, fe-guild and be-guild. People and agents load the same skills from it.

name: R&D brain
role: Reviewed pages about our systems, searchable by people and agents.
plain: The brain is a repo of short pages with owners and sources that explain how our systems work. People ask it through Slack; agents search it with the kb tool.

name: Golden-set repo
role: Restricted repo with eval answers that agents can never read.
plain: Hidden tests, human fixes and logs used to score agents live in a restricted repo. An agent's one-repo token never covers it, so an agent cannot see the answers.

name: TICKET-BENCH
role: 40 past fcp tickets with hidden tests, used to score Nova.
plain: A fixed set of real past tickets, each with a hidden test that proves the fix. Every harness change is scored on it before it ships.

name: BYTE-GOLD
role: Past PRs with known bugs, used to score Byte's reviews.
plain: A set of real and planted bugs in past PRs, labelled by people. Byte's prompt, model and playbook changes must not lower its score here.

name: ROUTINE-BENCH
role: Past red builds, broken updates and bugs, used to score routines.
plain: Each case is a past failure with the human fix next to it. A routine moves up the trust ladder only when its slice passes with no fake fixes.

name: BRAIN-QA
role: 60 real questions with source pages, used to score the brain.
plain: Real questions people asked, each with the page that answers it. It checks that search finds the right page and that answers are correct.

name: #ai-agents-alerts
role: Slack channel for platform alerts and hand-offs to people.
plain: Dead machines, blocked web requests, storms of red builds and services that are down are posted here. A person on DevOps or Platform looks.

name: Runs bucket
role: S3 bucket with each run's transcript, notes and proof.
plain: Everything a run saves lives under its own folder in this bucket: the session transcript, notes, screenshots and videos. Files expire after 30 days.

name: fcp-runner-set
role: Our own GitHub Actions runners inside the internal cluster.
plain: Most product CI jobs run on these self-hosted runners. Because they sit inside our network, a small Action there can reach internal services.

name: config/people.yaml
role: File mapping each person's Slack, Jira and GitHub names.
plain: It lists about 25 people with their Slack ID, Jira account and GitHub login, plus routine owners and reviewer rotations. Swaps are one-line PRs.

name: Requester
role: The person who handed the work to an agent; never its approver.
plain: The requester is whoever assigned the ticket to Nova, or the owner of a routine. They approve the plan, but they can never be the one who approves the PR.

name: Routine owner
role: Named person who answers for one routine.
plain: Each routine has one owner, written as the requester on its PRs. The owner gets its drafts in the early stage and can pause or resume it.

name: Reviewer of the day
role: Rotating teammate who reviews routine PRs that day.
plain: Each team keeps a short rotation. When a routine PR is ready, the reviewer of the day is asked, never the routine's owner.

name: Sean
role: Platform lead; builds this course's platform and requests pilot tickets.
plain: Sean leads the agent platform work and is the requester in most examples. He also reads the weekly bypass list and Nova review.

name: Nave
role: Maintains Byte, FCP Lab, Vanil and n8n; hands them over in G0.
plain: Nave built Byte and FCP Lab and is today the only person who can fix them. Part of the plan is for a second maintainer to learn them from him.

name: Shai
role: Owns the R&D brain, the developer survey and the trainings.
plain: Shai builds the brain pages and their tools, runs the developer survey and leads the trainings. His brain tooling is in Python.

name: Ronen
role: Security; decides data rules, threat model and the agents' access.
plain: Ronen is our security lead. He decides what data agents may see, leads the threat model and reviews every change to an agent's access.

name: Nir
role: Leadership; agrees the review rules and can break glass with Tal.
plain: Nir signs off on the review rules with Tal. He is one of the two people who may merge an urgent production fix without the usual approval.

name: Tal
role: Leadership; agrees the review rules and can break glass with Nir.
plain: Tal signs off on the review rules with Nir. Both are in the small break-glass team that can bypass the main-branch rules in an emergency.

name: Andy
role: Knows our Temporal setup; reviews the ai-agents Temporal install.
plain: Andy already runs Temporal for the product. He reviews the infrastructure PR that sets up the agents' own Temporal.

name: Dana
role: Made-up teammate in examples; approves PRs she did not request.
plain: Dana is not a real colleague; lessons use her as the teammate who reviews. In the RH-1234 story she is the one approval.

name: Omer
role: Made-up teammate in examples; asks Byte for a fix.
plain: Omer is a made-up reviewer in the Byte fix-mode examples. He is not a real colleague.

name: Lior
role: Made-up teammate in examples.
plain: Lior is a made-up name used in a few examples. He is not a real colleague.

name: Platform
role: Team that builds the agent platform; owns most tickets.
plain: Tickets marked [Platform] are written for the platform team, which is where the reader of this course sits. It owns the TypeScript services and the harness.

name: DevOps
role: Owns cloud accounts, infrastructure repo, Vault and runners.
plain: DevOps builds and approves everything in the infrastructure repo, and keeps Vault, the runners and the internal cluster running. People on DevOps run every apply.

name: Security
role: Decides data scope, reviews walls, runs the threat model.
plain: Security decides what agents may see and touch and checks that the walls are in the right places. Ronen leads it.

name: Guilds (FE, BE)
role: Frontend and backend engineers; review agent PRs and own skills.
plain: The FE guild and BE guild are the product engineers. They review agent PRs, write the codebase skills, label benchmarks and own the routines.

name: fcp-break-glass
role: Two-person team allowed to bypass main's rules in an emergency.
plain: Tal and Nir are the only members. Every bypass is logged and read weekly.
